study type: Prospective cohort study with a nested randomized controlled trial (for SET groups) and a retrospective control group.
exposure: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels (normal vs. slightly elevated) in the first trimester
Levothyroxine treatment for slightly elevated TSH
cohort: Pregnant women (n=1745) were categorized into three groups based on first-trimester TSH levels ('normal' or 'slightly elevated') and treatment status (levothyroxine treated or untreated for SET).
finding: Treatment with levothyroxine for slightly elevated TSH levels in pregnancy did not reverse the observed decrease in natural deliveries and increase in induced deliveries, despite achieving appropriate TSH levels in later trimesters.
mod_finding: Patients with slightly elevated TSH levels had significantly fewer natural deliveries and more induced deliveries compared to those with normal TSH, irrespective of levothyroxine treatment.
